content.text: {"mode":"team","summary":"The server and split math are already in place, so Pixel Pete builds the page and its live updates, Twinkle styles it, and I add server tests and check everything works together.","subtasks":[{"text":"Build the page form and live result","assignee":"a-pete","brief":"You own public/index.html and public/app.js. The page has three labelled inputs: bill amount (id \"bill\"), tip % (id \"tipPercent\", starts at 15) and number of people (id \"people\", starts at 1). Below them is a result area (id \"result\") showing Tip, Total and Each person pays. app.js is an ES module. It does `import { splitBill } from '/split.js'` and must not contain its own copy of the math. On every input event, pass the raw field values to splitBill. If the result is ok, show the amounts as money with 2 decimals. If not, hide the numbers and show its friendly message in an element with class \"message\", and add the class \"invalid\" to the input the error points to. Use these class names so the styling fits: \"field\" on each label+input wrapper, \"result\", \"result-row\", \"result-total\" (the each-person line), \"message\" and \"invalid\". Link /styles.css in the head and add a viewport meta tag. Done when, with `npm start` running, typing in any field updates the result right away, and empty or bad input shows a message instead of NaN.","parallel":true},{"text":"Style the page: calm, readable, phone-friendly","assignee":"a-twinkle","brief":"You own public/styles.css only. Style a single centered card with a title, three labelled inputs and a result area. Use these class names: \"field\" (wraps one label and its input), \"result\", \"result-row\" (one label and amount line: Tip, Total), \"result-total\" (the Each person pays line, the biggest and clearest), \"message\" (a friendly hint shown when input is missing or wrong, gentle, not alarming red) and \"invalid\" (on an input with a problem: a soft highlight). Keep it calm and readable with good contrast. It should look right on a 360px-wide phone with nothing scrolling sideways, and use large tap targets. Use system fonts and no external files. Done when the page looks clean on both a phone and a laptop."},{"text":"Test the server serves the page files, then put it all together","assignee":"a-semic","brief":"I own server.js and server.test.js. First, add node:test checks that /, /app.js, /styles.css and /split.js return 200 with the right content types. Then I merge Pete's and Twinkle's work, run `npm test` (all tests pass, still no dependencies) and `npm start`, and check in a browser that the page updates as you type and shows friendly messages for bad input. Done when the run command serves a working page and every test passes.","parallel":false}]}
